workflow.name: Product photo studio
workflow.description: Turns a product photo URL or description into clean e-commerce shots (white background, lifestyle, flat lay) with fal.ai. Optional background removal first. One image per scene, max 4. Images land in Artifacts.

inputs.name: product
inputs.label: Product photo URL (https://...) or a product description

inputs.name: style
inputs.label: Brand style or notes (optional, e.g. warm minimal, pastel, premium)

inputs.name: remove_bg
inputs.label: Remove the background from the photo first

nodes.label: Prepare the product
nodes.prompt:
Prepare the product reference for a photo shoot. Use curl; read the key from the FAL_KEY environment variable and never print it. If FAL_KEY is not set, stop and say: add FAL_KEY in Hive › Keys.

Product input:
{{inputs.product}}

Remove background: {{inputs.remove_bg}}

1. If the input contains an image URL (http/https), download it to "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/source.<ext>" (keep its real extension: png, jpg or webp) and look at it. Otherwise there is no source image: skip to step 3.
2. Only if a source image exists AND remove background is true: POST https://fal.run/fal-ai/birefnet with headers `Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY` and `Content-Type: application/json` and JSON {"image_url": <the product URL>}. The response is {"image": {"url": ...}}; download image.url into "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/cutout.png". This is one call; do not retry more than once.
3. Reply in exactly this format and nothing else:
REFERENCE_URL: <the cutout image.url if made, else the original product image URL, else none>
PRODUCT: <a precise 1-3 sentence visual description of the product: type, shape, materials, colors, finish, labels/text visible, proportions>

nodes.label: Write scene prompts
Render the shots with fal
nodes.prompt:
Render each scene prompt below with the fal.ai REST API: exactly one image per line, at most 4 images in total. Use curl with headers `Authorization: Key $FAL_KEY` and `Content-Type: application/json`; read the key from the FAL_KEY environment variable and never print it. If FAL_KEY is not set, stop and say: add FAL_KEY in Hive › Keys.

Pick the model from the REFERENCE_URL in the product notes:
- REFERENCE_URL is a URL: POST https://fal.run/fal-ai/flux-pro/kontext with JSON {"prompt": <scene prompt, phrased as: place this exact product in ...>, "image_url": <REFERENCE_URL>, "num_images": 1, "aspect_ratio": <"1:1" for square_hd, "3:4" for portrait_4_3, "4:3" for landscape_4_3; size is {{inputs.size}}>} (FLUX.1 Kontext [pro]; it takes aspect_ratio, not image_size). This keeps the real product and changes only the scene.
- REFERENCE_URL is none: POST https://fal.run/fal-ai/flux/dev (FLUX.1 [dev]) with JSON {"prompt": <scene prompt>, "image_size": "{{inputs.size}}", "num_images": 1}.

For each line, download images[0].url into "$ARTIFACTS_DIR/shot-<scene-slug>.png". If one call fails, retry it once, then move on and note the failure (never more than 8 image calls in total).

Reply with one line per scene: <saved path> | <model used> | <prompt used>.

Product notes:
{{prep.output}}

Scene prompts:
{{prompts.output}}
